blocks.text: This video shows how to put an animation from Pixodesk SVG Animator on a plain web page. It takes one script and one element, with no build step. Let's start with the page as it is.

blocks.alt: A heading, and nothing that moves yet.

blocks.text: A heading, and nothing that moves yet. To play animations, the page needs the Pixodesk player. Let's copy it into the project.

blocks.alt: One command copied the player script into the folder.

blocks.text: One command copied the player script into the folder. Now for the animation itself. Let's switch to the editor, where a football is already drawn.

blocks.alt: It's a vector drawing, standing still.

blocks.text: It's a vector drawing, standing still. To make it move, let's switch on Auto mode.

blocks.alt: With Auto mode on, every change becomes a keyframe.

blocks.text: With Auto mode on, every change becomes a keyframe. Half a second in, let's drag the ball down to the floor.

blocks.alt: A keyframe appears on the timeline, holding the new position.

blocks.text: A keyframe appears on the timeline, holding the new position. At one second, let's bring it back up.

blocks.alt: Now it falls and rises again, in one second.

blocks.text: Now it falls and rises again, in one second. A real ball speeds up as it falls, and slows down as it rises. Let's set that easing.

blocks.alt: Gravity easing, falling and rising, makes the bounce feel natural.

blocks.text: Gravity easing, falling and rising, makes the bounce feel natural. One bounce is not enough, so let's loop the animation.

blocks.alt: Loop is saved with the file, so the animation repeats forever.

blocks.text: Loop is saved with the file, so the animation repeats forever.

blocks.alt: The animation is ready. Let's save it as JSON, next to the page.

blocks.text: The animation is ready. Let's save it as JSON, next to the page.

blocks.alt: The animation file is already there, next to the page.

blocks.text: The animation file is already there, next to the page. Let's load the player, at the end of the page.

blocks.alt: The script tag loads the player, and one call finds every animation on the page.

blocks.text: The script tag loads the player, and one call finds every animation on the page. Then, let's add an element that names the animation file.

blocks.alt: Its data attribute points at the file. The player plays it as the file says, starting on load and repeating forever.

blocks.text: Its data attribute points at the file. The player plays it as the file says, starting on load and repeating forever. Let's reload the page, and watch.

blocks.alt: There it is. The ball bounces, on a plain web page.

blocks.text: There it is. The ball bounces, on a plain web page. So, one copied script, one file saved from the editor, and one element. That's all it takes to bring an animation onto a web page.
